review_findings_resolved.resolution: Marked Skill.canonicalKey @unique (Page 03 §1 ERD, starter table, §4.2, §6.1 constraint table). Restated the BR-18 single-record key precisely: @@unique([employeeId,skillId]) is necessary-but-not-sufficient; canonicalKey @unique collapses aliases ('TypeScript'/'TS') to one canonical Skill.id. Added §3.4 documenting how resolveCanonicalSkill resolves cert/resume/self-service names to the canonical key before the EmployeeSkill upsert. ADR-007 Decision/Alternatives/Impact updated.

Specified a de-dupe failure fallback on the P0 cert-confirm write path. skill-identity is now a Claude merge ADVISOR (Layer 2), not a gate; the deterministic canonicalKey (Layer 1) is the always-available persistence key. On skill-identity failure/unreachable/invalid-JSON, fall back to create-new keyed by canonicalKey + reconcilePending flag — write never blocks or corrupts; canonicalKey @unique keeps it single-record under concurrency. Documented in Page 03 §3.4, Page 02 §4.1 sequence + note + §5 cross-cutting row, ADR-007.

Pinned runMatch transport as a READ. Removed it from the Server Actions (mutations) table; added Page 02 §3.2a specifying it as a read-only Route Handler (POST /api/match, query in body, no DB writes) with GET-equivalent acceptable; rationale covers why not a Server Action and caching/idempotency cleanliness. ADR-006 Decision/Rationale updated.

Added DB-level upload idempotency: @@unique([employeeId, contentHash]) on both Certificate and Resume (scoped per employee). App-layer 'seen before?' check kept as fast path; the unique constraint is the race-safe backstop under concurrent double-submit. Updated Page 03 ERD field comments, §4.6, §6.1 constraint table; Page 02 §5 cross-cutting row; ADR-004 Decision/Rationale/Impact.

key_design_decisions: Single canonical EmployeeSkill record with monotonic trust-state promotion (self-reported->manager-approved->verified), upsert keyed by (profileId, canonicalSkillId); Skill.canonicalKey @unique enforces one canonical Skill per concept so aliases (TypeScript/TS) cannot fan out into duplicate rows — the BR-18 invariant the hero loop depends on (ADR-007, TS-001).

Skill de-dupe is resilient on the P0 write path: deterministic canonicalKey is the persistence key, Claude skill-identity only advises merges; on de-dupe failure, create-new + reconcile-later — the verified cert write never blocks/corrupts (TS-002).

Upload idempotency is DB-enforced via @@unique([employeeId, contentHash]) on Certificate/Resume, not just an app-layer check (TS-004); the staffing search runMatch is a read-only Route Handler, not a mutation (TS-003).
All intelligence routes through one Claude wrapper enforcing Zod-before-write; failures return typed errors and write nothing (ADR-003, P2).
Real Google OAuth restricted to nulogic.io with a seeded synthetic-handle->profile mapping; real email discarded after hd check, zero real PII persisted (ADR-001/005).
Prompt caching of the system prompt + serialized profile dataset across match queries and the loop's before/after run (P7/BR-12).
Single Next.js 16 app using proxy.ts (renamed middleware) and async cookies()/headers()/params — verified against node_modules/next/dist/docs/ (ADR-006, P9).
open_items: UX/Figma designs were 'in progress' at PRD time — UI sections (Phase 8) describe a minimal clean NULogic-branded surface; refine when designs land (delta trigger for Page 02 frontend/UX).
Confidence threshold for cert/resume parse gating is a tuning constant to be set during Phase 2/5.
Migration history deferred (db:push only) — acceptable for MVP per ADR-002; revisit if persistence outlives the demo.

skill-identity de-dupe failures create a reconcilePending Skill row (TS-002 fallback); a periodic/manual reconcile pass to merge such rows is deferred — degrades de-dupe quality only, never loop correctness.
